ai.description: This snake reaches 40–50 cm. It is reddish-brown dorsally with a distinct, dark V-shaped mark on the nape and a pale, unpatterned belly. It lacks a loreal scale.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Oligodon kheriensis* is the presence of a distinct, V-shaped dark marking on the nape, which is absent in similar kukri snakes.
ai.habitat: The Coral Red Kukri Snake inhabits the moist deciduous forests and terai grasslands of the Himalayan foothills, typically at elevations below 500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Coral Red Kukri Snake is primarily nocturnal and uses its specialized, blade-like teeth to slice into reptile eggs, allowing it to consume the contents efficiently.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Oligodon kheriensis* is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–6 eggs. Breeding occurs during the pre-monsoon season, typically from April to June in northern India.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Oligodon kheriensis* is endemic to the Terai region of northern India, specifically recorded in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar at low elevations along the Himalayan foothills.
